tiers.VERIFIED-RUNTIME: a probe stdout line proves it on hython 22.0.400 (pxr resolution)
tiers.FIXTURE-VERIFIED: the b6 SOP component proves it on the actual file
tiers.DOC-STATED: read from the blueprint / shipped skill text; unverified here

checker_contract: for every VERIFIED-RUNTIME/FIXTURE-VERIFIED row, anchor is 'stdout.txt:<N>' and BOTH 'arc=<arc>' and the 'verify' token appear verbatim on that line; PROPOSED/DOC-STATED rows carry a doc anchor (no stdout.txt:<N>) and are skipped.

rows.rule: The world root prim is tagged kind=component: one Marble world is exactly one component model, the leaf of the model hierarchy (assembly > group > component). The SOP USD Create Component authors it on the wrapper Xform.
rows.why: kind is a local metadata opinion (not a composition arc). component (not assembly/group) because the world has no sub-model children to own; kind=component is what makes Usd.ModelAPI treeIteration and a spatial-lane organization walk (blueprint sec.3.3 I3.a/I3.b) stop at the world as one queryable unit.

rows.rule: The collider mesh subtree sits under a Scope authored purpose=proxy (/geo/proxy). Structure travels on the proxy purpose.
rows.why: purpose is an inherited-down local attribute, not a composition arc. proxy (not default/guide) so the viewport can draw the light collider (~47k tris on the lane fixture) while Karma consumes the render splat; prevents the viewport from moving 2M splat points every frame (viewport re-cook failure).

rows.rule: The splat subtree sits under a Scope authored purpose=render (/geo/render). Appearance travels on the render purpose.
rows.why: render (not default) so the heavy splat is only realised at render time by the delegate that wants it; a viewer set to proxy purpose never realises it. Purpose is authored on the Scope, not the leaf (see purpose-splat-inherited).

rows.topic: splat Points purpose is inherited, not authored on the leaf
rows.rule: The Points prim /geo/render/points_0 authors NO purpose (authored=default) yet computes purpose=render, inherited down namespace from the /geo/render Scope.
rows.why: purpose is one of USD's inherited-down attributes: setting it once on the render Scope covers every leaf beneath it. Authoring purpose=render on each leaf would be redundant and drift-prone. The SOP build proves the inheritance path, correcting the blueprint sec.2.5 sketch which draws purpose on /splat itself.

rows.topic: shot composes the world by payload (splat + collider together)
rows.rule: The shot references /WL_<world_id> by PAYLOAD, not reference. Payloading the real 19.8 MB component then Unload drops 9 prims; Load restores them.
rows.why: payload = reference + unloadable. The 2M-splat SH data (~360 MB) must be droppable from an open stage so the shot opens and the layout tools work on the light collider without the appearance resident. FIXTURE-VERIFIED on the actual component file.

rows.topic: the composed shot prim carries a payload arc
rows.rule: Usd.PrimCompositionQuery on the shot prim reports a payload composition arc (arcs: root,payload).
rows.why: confirms the arc that composes the world into the shot is a payload, the mechanism unload/load acts on.

rows.rule: Runtime: stage.Unload on a payloaded prim removes its subtree (unloadable=True); the same Unload on a referenced prim does nothing (unloadable=False).
rows.why: the neighbour arc is reference (identical namespace mapping, one step stronger in LIVRPS). Reference is rejected at the shot seam solely because it cannot be unloaded: a referenced 2M-splat world is resident for the life of the stage. This is the single property that decides payload over reference.

rows.topic: the SOP-built component authors zero variant sets
rows.rule: The USD Create Component output carries 0 variantSets across all prims. splatTier / surface / physics variants are PROPOSED authoring, not present in the fixture.
rows.why: keeps the tiering honest: the blueprint sec.2.5 variant sets are a proposal; the shipped SOP path does not author them, so their rows below are PROPOSED, not FIXTURE-VERIFIED.

rows.topic: the SOP-built component authors no customData:worldlabs
rows.rule: The component root customData holds only ['userDocBrief']; no worldlabs provenance key is present.
rows.why: again keeps tiering honest: customData:worldlabs provenance (blueprint sec.2.5) is PROPOSED, not authored by the SOP build. A later authoring step adds it.

rows.rule: One attribute carrying all six opinions resolves strong->weak as local>inherit>variant>reference>payload>specialize; composed value = the local opinion.
rows.why: the empirical ladder every arc choice in this record reasons from. Matches the shipped skill's stated order (solaris-usd-composition.md) -- confirmed, not recited.

rows.rule: A reference opinion wins over a payload opinion on the same attribute (adjacent in the ladder).
rows.why: explains why the world is authored as a self-contained payload TARGET and the shot uses the weaker payload seam: had the shot used reference, it would compose one step stronger AND be non-unloadable. The strength asymmetry and the unload asymmetry point the same way.

rows.rule: A payload opinion wins over a specialize opinion on the same attribute.
rows.why: bounds the ladder from below: only specialize is weaker than payload. Any per-world fallback you want the shot to override cheaply belongs on specialize, never on the payload.

rows.rule: Specialize loses to every other opinion; it supplies fallbacks that any stronger arc overrides.
rows.why: the correct reading of the arc the deep-dive got wrong. Use specialize for base templates whose values must always yield to a real opinion, never for something that must survive an override.

rows.rule: spot1 with a local intensity=2.0 that specializes a base keeps 2.0 after the base changes to 0.5. The deep-dive's 'spot1 gets 0.5 (base is stronger)' is false; the prim's own local opinion wins over what it specializes.
rows.why: the CTO note flagged this line as deliberately wrong; the probe settles it. A local opinion always beats a specialized base -- specialize only fills in where the prim itself is silent.

rows.rule: For inherit list-editing, the first-added inherit is the strongest: /Obj inheriting A(=10) then B(=20) composes to 10.0.
rows.why: the CTO note left this 'unverified'; on 22.0.400 the claim holds (default AddInherit prepends at the back of the prepend list, so earlier adds sit in front / stronger). Recorded VERIFIED-RUNTIME, not assumed.

rows.rule: PROPOSED: a splatTier variant set on /WL_<world_id> selecting the 2M-splat full tier vs the 500k low tier.
rows.why: variant (not two separate payloads, not reference swap) because a variant selection switches representation without recomposing the stack or re-opening a file, and rides ABOVE reference/payload in the ladder so the shot's selection wins over anything the component ships. Not present in the SOP build (see variantsets-absent-in-sop-build); this is proposed authoring.

rows.rule: PROPOSED (gated G-1): a physics variant set applying UsdPhysicsCollisionAPI to /geo/collider under the collision variant, none otherwise.
rows.why: variant so a sim-ready export toggles the collision schema without a second asset; kept OFF the critical path behind gate G-1 (blueprint sec.9) -- no Isaac Sim evidence sought here. Not authored by the SOP build.

rows.rule: PROPOSED: customData:worldlabs = {world_id, model, frame, semantics_metadata, source_urls, applied} on /WL_<world_id>.
rows.why: customData (a local metadata dict) not a typed schema, because the provenance is SYNAPSE-private, travels with the prim through reference/payload, and must not collide with vendor USD schemas. The 'applied' sub-block is what makes the frame conversion idempotent (see transforms-baked-not-xform). Not authored by the SOP build (see customdata-worldlabs-absent-in-sop-build).

rows.rule: PROPOSED: the world component is NOT marked instanceable.
rows.why: instanceable=true would collapse the prim to a shared prototype: (1) there is exactly one instance of each world, so instancing buys nothing; (2) an instanceable prim cannot carry per-instance variant selection (splatTier/surface) or per-instance overrides, which the shot needs; (3) instance proxies complicate the payload unload path. instanceable is a local metadata flag; default false is correct. No runtime anchor -- a design decision.
rows.anchor: reasoning: blueprint sec.2.5 (one world = one component) + LIVRPS ladder

rows.topic: metric / ground / chirality transforms live baked in the file, not as an Xform on the payload
rows.rule: PROPOSED: the metric+ground and axis (chirality) conversions are BAKED into the exported splat/collider geometry and recorded in customData:worldlabs.applied; they are NOT re-applied as an Xform op on /WL_<world_id> in the shot layer.
rows.why: the failure this prevents is the DOUBLE TRANSFORM: a file already converted to metric+Y-up, then wrapped in a live Xform that converts again, is scaled and flipped twice. Baking once + an 'applied' ledger (idempotent per blueprint I2.d) means a re-open never re-converts. A live Xform op would also be a local opinion the shot could clobber. Placement Xforms (positioning the world in the shot) are a SEPARATE, legitimate Xform in the shot layer.

rows.rule: DOC-STATED: convert in the order metric+ground -> axis (180 about X) -> Houdini Y-up; 'applied' flags make it idempotent (blueprint sec.2.7, WL-API-03).
rows.why: order is a vendor claim (WL-API-03), not a preference: metric+ground operate in the raw OpenCV frame, the axis flip comes after. Recorded DOC-STATED -- not runtime-verified in this leg (no fixture round-trip through the full conversion here).

rows.topic: why the world is heavy enough to payload
rows.rule: DOC-STATED: a 2M-splat world carries ~45 floats/point of spherical harmonics (~360 MB at 2M, ~90 MB at 500k); this is the weight that makes payload (not reference) mandatory.
rows.why: blueprint sec.2.5 property 3. The SH payload size is the physical reason the appearance must be unloadable; the runtime unload asymmetry (payload-vs-reference-unloadable) is the mechanism that delivers it.
